title: Sitting in with a modern 16-piece band and the New York offer
summary: A visiting arranged band needed a chord pianist; he excelled, was offered $25 a night to go to New York but declined from nerves.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Mrs. Kimball was a piano player, her husband. With Celestan. Yeah. He used to play with Celestan too, but at that time he was playing with Sidney. And they had a wonderful band. And I'm telling you the truth Bill, those people really, they learned me something. Because when I got with that band, I could play the chords, but Sidney had a lot of stock arrangement, they didn't write chords out too much. And man they used to cut me every night. I was working 24 hours a day with the band because I had to take two, three numbers home every night and practice all day until I finally made it with the band. And I become one of the best piano players that he had because I played the way he wanted. And I played the rhythm and just in orchestration a little part would come in for the piano and I'd study that and I'd be able to make it. I remember an experience I had one time that Morton and Moulin came down with an old 16 piece band and they didn't have any piano player. And the leader of the band at that time, I forget his name, Ag Sidney could have used me. And man I told him, I said listen man, Sidney's band was bad enough, I mean the music they had. And these guys was playing strictly arrangements you know, they were really more modern than Sidney's band. And I told him man I couldn't make it. So he said oh come on and try you know. So fortunately when I got up there all the music was written in chords you know. And when they ever had a solo for the piano they just had a solo and you had to break the chord.
And that was right up my alley man.

So we were getting I think $13, Sidney had two bands. Sidney got $13, they played before the other band. And this band was getting $20. So I worked both bands that night and I played so well with this band because they were fellows were getting off you know, there was modern saxophone playing trumpets getting off. And all they wanted was somebody to chord. Well I had got my experience from this first place job I worked at the Pelican by letting these fellows jam and chord with them. See and they loved the way I played. And he offered to give me $25 a night for 32 dates. They were going up to New York and I got cold feet and I wouldn't take it. I had heard so much about these New York musicians I was afraid to go you know. So I worked all around Bourbon until George went to New York with Bump. And I know you remember I went to New York with them.
